query: Which material can be used for superconducting properties, and why?

generation.conditions: Temperature varied from above room temperature down to below 40 K in a low-vibration, cryogenic environment

generation.baseline: Normal metallic conduction with finite resistance above the superconducting transition temperature
generation.boundary: Superconducting properties may diminish if impurity levels or structural defects exceed a critical threshold, or if stoichiometry deviates significantly from the ideal MgB2 composition
generation.uncertainty: Exact critical temperature and the sensitivity of the superconducting properties to minor synthesis imperfections require further empirical clarification
